newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-BURNING BECKER SCRAMBLED BY SPANIARD.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BURNING BECKER SCRAMBLED BY SPANIARD.

text.p: Boris Becker couldn't take the heat at the Australian Open on Monday and suffered as a young Spaniard scrambled his title defence.
Becker lost a five-set tussle on centre court to 20-year-old Carlos Moya on the first day of the championships on Monday.
"My brain is like scrambled eggs," said the 29-year-old German, describing his mental condition after a match lasting three hours and 31 minutes on centre court.

"I'm really struggling to talk normally because I'm burning, especially my feet and legs are really hot," said Becker, who described Moya, ranked 25, as a dangerous threat before the tournament began.
The defeat heightens Becker's reputation as the most vulnerable of the world's elite players in the early rounds of grand slam tournaments.
It is the third time in his past four appearances in Melbourne that the 29-year-old German, a six-times winner of grand slam tournaments, has made a first-round exit.
Becker said he struggled for timing as Moya recovered from two sets to one down to triumph 5-7 7-6 (7-4) 3-6 6-1 6-4.
"There were times when I could not really move at all because I was afraid I would lose the skin on my feet," Becker said.
The air temperatures reached 32 degrees celsius during the day and soared even higher at courtside because of the heat-absorbing hardcourt playing surface.

"It was extremely hard out there," said Becker, who described his first round pairing with Moya, a losing finalist to Britain's Tim Henman in the Sydney International ATP event on Saturday, as a stroke of bad luck.
"I knew that this was going to be the toughest first round match in the draw and as it turned out is was my last match," Becker said.
Becker also lost to Moya in their only previous meeting at last year's Paris Open.
World number two and second seed Michael Chang, in contrast to Becker, promptly dispatched Belgian qualifier Kris Goossens on Monday.
Pete Sampras, the top seed and world number one, faces another qualifier, Dinu Pescariu of Romania, in their first round match on Tuesday.
"Seeing the draw that the other top guys got, it is obviously more difficult to play a guy like Moya than someone who has had to qualify.
"But Carlos was the better man today and he deserved to win," said Becker, who beat Chang in the final in Melbourne in 1996 to end a barren five years without a grand slam win.

Asked if he would play for Germany in next month' Davis Cup tie against Spain, Becker joked: "Are you kidding me? They have about 10 Moyas out there waiting for me. My legs are not that fresh any more."
